In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Tin

It is Meccan.

It is established by the narration of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this surah in the Maghrib prayer; Muslim recorded it in his Sahih.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾. Mujahid and al-Hasan said: it is the fig that is eaten and the olive that is pressed.

The meaning: "By the Lord of the fig and the olive."

Qatadah said: the fig is the mountain on which Damascus lies, and the olive is the mountain on which Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) lies.

Ka'b said: it is Damascus and Bayt al-Maqdis.

al-Farra' related that they are two mountains between Hulwan and Hamadhan.

It is also said: he intended the places where the fig and the olive grow.

al-Nahhas said: this view contradicts the apparent meaning of the verse, and no one whose statement would be a proof has been reported to hold it.

Wa-qawluhu: ﴿Wa-ṭūri Sīnīn﴾ — most of the exegetes say that it is the mountain on which God spoke to Moses.

It is also established from ʿUmar that he recited: "Wa-ṭūri Saynāʾ," and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "Wa-ṭūri Sīnāʾ," with a kasra on the sīn.

Al-Ḥasan said: al-Ṭūr is the mountain, and Sīnīn: the blessed.

And from al-Akhfash: Ṭūr: the name of the mountain, and Sīnīn: the name of the tree.
And His saying: ﴿And this secure land﴾ is Makkah, by consensus (ijma'), and the meaning of "al-amin" (the secure) is: safe is whoever is within it.

The words of Allah, ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature﴾, are the answer to the oath.

Mujahid, Ibrahim and a group [of scholars] said: "in the best of stature" means "in the best of form."

It was also said: "in the best of stature" refers to his being well-proportioned and balanced.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 95, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. Mujahid and al-Hasan said: "To the Fire, except those who believed."

According to this, the verse concerns the disbelievers.

It has also been said that it was revealed concerning a specific disbeliever, and it is said that he was Abu Jahl.

It is said that he was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.

And it has been said that it was others besides them.

Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i), al-Dahhak and a group said: "Then We return him to the lowest of the low" means: the most decrepit age (ardhal al-'umr), and "the lowest" are the weak, the sick and the frail elderly.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 95, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿Except those who believe﴾. The exception (al-istithna') is problematic in this surah. According to the view of al-Hasan and Mujahid, the exception is apparent, and the meaning is: "We return people to the Fire, except those who believed and did righteous deeds, for they are not returned to the Fire." The meaning of "al-insan" (man) here is: people.

As for the view of Ibrahim and al-Dahhak, the exception is problematic according to this opinion. This was said by al-Nahhas.

The meaning according to this view is: "Except those who believe, so they are not returned to the lowest state of life (ardhal al-'umr)." Its meaning is that their righteous deeds are recorded for them after old age as they used to perform them in youth, even if they become unable to perform them. Thus it is as if they were not returned to the lowest state of life. This meaning has been related from Ibrahim, and it has been narrated in some reports, traced back (marfu') to the Messenger (ﷺ).

And His saying: ﴿So for them is a reward that will not be cut off﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions. The first: no one bestows a favor upon them (other than Allah) with a reminder that spoils the blessing upon them.

The well-known opinion: "not cut off," and this supports the interpretation we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 95, verse 7:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So what makes you deny the Judgment after this?﴾ The meaning: So what makes you deny, O doubter, the Day of Reckoning, after you have witnessed what you have witnessed of the power of God, Most High. This is the well-known view.

There is another view regarding the verse, that its meaning is: "So who denies you of the Judgment after this?" addressed to the Prophet, i.e., who is it that denies you of the Day of Reckoning after the proofs and signs that have become manifest have become manifest. This was related by Abu Mu'adh al-Nahwi (a grammarian). The first view is preferable, because "ma" (what) in the sense of "man" (who) is remote in linguistic usage.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 95, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ is an interrogative (istifham) with the meaning of affirmation (tahqiq), like the saying of Jarir:

(Are you not the best of those who rode the mounts, / and the most generous of the peoples in the bellies of the (wine) skins?)

That is: "You are indeed so."

It has been reported from a group of the Companions that when they finished the surah they would say: "Allahumma bala" (O Allah, yes), and in another narration: "Bala, and I am of those who bear witness to that." Among them were Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.
